design.descriptor: Option<i32> inherited_recall_fd on kernel SandboxSpec; borrowed raw descriptor, caller keeps socket open until spawn returns. Linux pre_exec copies fd and clears FD_CLOEXEC via F_GETFD/F_SETFD; parent flags unchanged. No fixed dup2 target needed because caller passes actual descriptor number in argv, matching spike --recall-fd.

premise_corrections.claim: Removing sendto/recvfrom must kill the child with SIGSYS(31)
premise_corrections.fact: Unknown syscalls return EPERM, not SIGSYS: HEAD security/sandbox/linux.rs:378-382. Actual probe exits 72/71 with errno1 and no signal. SIGSYS belongs to explicit hostile syscall list (linux.rs:345-363,391-400). This is an assignment/acceptance premise, not a false claim in ADR-060.

adr_060.observed: Inherited descriptor + child CLOEXEC clear + sendto/recvfrom work under real T2. No measured ADR amendment premise was disproved. Same-uid descriptor theft and Yama sufficiency were not re-proven here; ptrace_scope was observed as 1.
